revenue_model.pricing_strategy: Value-based pricing anchored on regulatory risk and compliance cost savings

recommended_scenario.rationale: Base case balances growth speed with capital efficiency. 12 customers in Year 1 is achievable with focused sales on Top 50 banks. Break-even at month 14 with $2.1M capital gives runway for GTM ramp without excessive burn. Conservative scenario is too slow (18 months burn); aggressive requires exceptional sales execution (22 customers) and higher cash requirements.
critical_success_factors: Close 3-4 Top 50 bank customers in Year 1 (establishes reference customers)
Achieve $250K ACV on large bank segment (pricing holds at regulatory risk premium)
Maintain 75%+ gross margin (SaaS support costs must stay contained)
Monthly churn < 2% (customer retention critical for LTV model)
CAC stays below $120K (sales productivity must improve by Q3)
key_metrics_to_monitor: Sales cycle length (assumed 4 months, must validate)
Monthly churn rate (assumed 2%, needs early validation)
Gross margin trending (75% target, watch cloud and support costs)
Sales attainment to plan (must hit 3-4 deals Q3-Q4 Year 1)

assumptions: Pricing: Large banks willing to pay $250K annually (anchored in compliance cost savings of $1M+)
CAC: Sales & marketing cost $120K per customer (includes founder sales time, one sales hire, marketing)
LTV Churn: Monthly churn 2% (24% annual, typical for enterprise SaaS); 4-year lifetime assumption
Gross Margin: 75% sustainable (cloud infrastructure 15%, customer support 10% of revenue)
Sales Cycle: 4 months average (range 2-6 months depending on regulatory cycle)
Market Adoption: Large banks adopt as regulatory pressure increases (timing assumption in Vol 1)
data_gaps: Actual willingness-to-pay from bank customer interviews (using Vol 2 estimates as proxy)
Competitive pricing (Regulatory AI and ModelWatch pricing not public)
Sales productivity benchmarks for compliance software (using SaaS benchmarks as proxy)
Implementation services revenue opportunity (not modeled, potential upside)
Data exchange partnerships revenue (not modeled, potential future stream)
confidence_rationale: Unit economics are sound with strong LTV:CAC ratio (12.5x vs. 3x benchmark). Break-even timeline is realistic for enterprise SaaS. However, confidence is not higher because willingness-to-pay needs customer validation (using Vol 2 estimates), sales cycle assumptions need early validation (4 months is assumed but may vary), and competitive pricing is unknown. Model sensitivity to monthly churn assumption is high (3% churn moves break-even 6+ months). Base case recommended but requires tight execution on sales productivity.
